A company wants to create an AI solution to generate images and descriptions for a product catalog. The company needs to select a foundation model (FM) for this solution.

The company must consider the output types of each FM.

Which FM characteristic is the company evaluating?

comment.en: When a company is choosing a foundation model (FM) for an AI solution, it must consider what type of content or output the model can generate.That type of output is known as the model’s modality.
It must evaluate whether a candidate foundation model supports the required output modalities (image generation and text generation). The key characteristic under evaluation is therefore modality.

question.en:
A company wants to use an ML model to analyze customer reviews on social media. The model must determine if each review has a neutral, positive, or negative sentiment.

Which model evaluation strategy will meet these requirements?

comment.en: In Classification strategy (sentiment task), the model assigns each input text to a specific category. For instance, Positive, Negative & Neutral.

The problem is: • Input: customer review text • Output: neutral, positive, or negative This is a sentiment analysis task. Sentiment analysis is a type of multiclass classification, because the model must assign each text to one of several predefined categories.

question.en:
An online learning company with large volumes of education materials wants to use enterprise search.

Which AWS service meets these requirements?

comment.en: Amazon Kendra is AWS’s fully managed enterprise search service.
Amazon Kendra is an intelligent enterprise search service that allows users to search across large volumes of documents and contents using natural language.

question.en:
A company creates video content. The company wants to use generative AI to generate new creative content and to reduce video creation time.

Which solution will meet these requirements in the MOST operationally efficient way?

text.en: Use the Amazon Titan Image Generator model on Amazon Bedrock to generate intermediate images. Use video editing software to create videos.
Use the Amazon Nova Canvas model on Amazon Bedrock to generate intermediate images. Use video editing software to create videos.
Use the Amazon Nova Reel model on Amazon Bedrock to generate videos.
Use the Amazon Nova Pro model on Amazon Bedrock to generate videos.

comment.en: Amazon Nova Reel is specifically designed for video generation. It supports: • Direct AI-generated videos • High-quality motion generation • Creative video content creation • Minimal operational overhead (no stitching or image sequencing required) This makes it the MOST operationally efficient solution. >> Nova Pro is a text and multimodal LLM, not a video generation model.

Why C? Amazon Nova Reel It's a state-of-the-art video generation model. Using Amazon Nova Reel, you can produce short videos through text prompts and images, control visual style and pacing, and generate professional-quality video content for marketing, advertising, and entertainment. Ref: https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/aws/introducing-amazon-nova-frontier-intelligence-and-industry-leading-price-performance/
Using a model built specifically for video generation eliminates the need for additional image-generation and video-editing steps.

question.en:
A company is training ML models on datasets. The datasets contain some classes that have more examples than other classes. The company wants to measure how well the model balances detecting and labeling the classes.

Which metric should the company use?

comment.en: When the dataset is imbalanced (some classes have many more examples than others), metrics like accuracy become misleading. The company wants a metric that measures how well the model: • Detects each class (recall) • Correctly labels each class (precision) The F1 score is the harmonic mean of precision and recall. This makes it the best metric for imbalanced classification problems.
A high F1 score indicates a good balance between finding relevant instances and avoiding incorrect classifications.

question.en:
A company is analyzing financial transaction records. The company categorizes the records as either personal or business. The company inserts the categories into the transaction records.

Which data preparation step does this describe?

comment.en: Pretty self-explanatory for a supervised ML technique.

The company is: • Assigning categories (“personal” or “business”) • Adding those labels to the transaction records This is exactly what data labeling means—adding class labels or annotations to raw data so it can be used for supervised machine learning.

question.en:
A company is using Amazon SageMaker to deploy a model that identifies if social media posts contain certain topics. The company needs to show how different input features influence model behavior.

Which SageMaker feature meets these requirements?

comment.en: The company needs to show how different input features influence model behavior—this is a requirement for model explainability. SageMaker Clarify provides: • Feature attribution (e.g., SHAP values) • Explainability reports • Bias detection during training and inference • Tools to show which inputs most affect predictions
Straight forward SageMaker Clarify due to its following characteristics: - Explainability - Feature importance - Model transparency - Understanding predictions - Bias detection

question.en: Which AWS service or feature stores embeddings in a vector database for use with foundation models (FMs) and Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG)?

comment.en: Amazon OpenSearch Service supports vector search and can store and retrieve embeddings for RAG applications.
openseach supports embeddings (multi dimensional vectors)

question.en: Which scenario represents a practical use case for generative AI?

text.en: Using an ML model to forecast product demand
Employing a chatbot to provide human-like responses to customer queries in real time
Using an analytics dashboard to track website traffic and user behavior
Implementing a rule-based recommendation engine to suggest products to customers

comment.en: Except option B, none of any of the options are related with Generative AI as some are showing the references of predictive analytics and business intelligence and analytics and not AI content generation usecases.

Generative AI excels at producing new content, such as: • Human-like text • Conversations • Images • Code • Audio • Summaries A chatbot generating natural, conversational responses is a classic, practical generative AI use case.

question.en:
A company is using Amazon Bedrock for a generative AI solution. The solution must integrate a service with vector database storage and vector search capabilities.

Which AWS service will meet these requirements?

comment.en: For a generative AI solution using vector embeddings, the company needs: • Vector database storage • k-nearest neighbor (k-NN) search • Similarity search • Embedding search for RAG workflows Amazon OpenSearch Service provides all of these: ✔ Native vector search ✔ k-NN and ANN (HNSW, IVF) indexing ✔ Scalable vector storage ✔ Integration with RAG architectures and Amazon Bedrock
Correct answer: B. Amazon OpenSearch Service

question.en:
A company has developed an ML model to approve or reject loan applications. The model’s decision-making process must be transparent and explainable to comply with regulatory requirements. The company must document the decision-making process for audit purposes.

Which solution will meet these requirements?

comment.en: SageMaker Model Cards are specifically designed for: • Documenting how a model was built • Recording intended use cases • Describing model behavior and limitations • Capturing explainability and fairness considerations • Storing evaluation metrics • Supporting regulatory and audit requirements This is exactly what the company needs for a loan approval model, which is a highly regulated use case requiring transparency and documentation for audits.

question.en:
A company is building a new generative AI chatbot. The chatbot uses an Amazon Bedrock foundation model (FM) to generate responses. During testing, the company notices that the chatbot is prone to prompt injection attacks.

What can the company do to secure the chatbot with the LEAST implementation effort?

text.en: Fine-tune the FM to avoid harmful responses.
Use Amazon Bedrock Guardrails content filters and denied topics.
Change the FM to a more secure FM.
Use chain-of-thought prompting to produce secure responses.

comment.en: Core requirement of this usecase is "LEAST implementation effort", therefore -----> Bedrock Guardrails

Amazon Bedrock Guardrails provides built-in protection against: • Prompt injection attacks • Jailbreak prompts • Harmful or restricted topics • Unsafe user queries • Unsafe model outputs You can configure guardrails without retraining, without modifying the model, and without changing your application logic. This makes it the fastest and easiest way to secure a Bedrock-based chatbot.

question.en: What does inference refer to in the context of AI?

text.en: The process of creating new AI algorithms
The use of a trained model to make predictions or decisions on unseen data
The process of combining multiple AI models into one model
The method of collecting training data for AI systems

comment.en: Inference is what happens after a model is trained. During inference, the model: • Takes new, unseen input • Applies what it learned during training • Produces predictions, classifications, or decisions

question.en:

Which Amazon Bedrock feature or resource will meet these requirements?

The crux of the requirements in this question are: - Calling external APIs - Multi-step reasoning - Managing and manipulating response options - Take judgemental actions - Orchestrating workflows Which can get fulfiled through Amazon Bedrock Agents.

Use Amazon Rekognition to analyze image contents and detect text attributes.

Generate images from text as inputs (Text-to-image model) -----> Stable Diffusion model.
stable diffusion is for illustrations.

question.en:
A company acquires International Organization for Standardization (ISO) accreditation to manage AI risks and to use AI responsibly.

What does this accreditation reflect about the company?

text.en: All members of the company are ISO certified.
All AI systems that the company uses are ISO certified.
All AI application team members are ISO certified.
The company’s development framework is ISO certified.

comment.en: ISO accreditation does not certify: • individual employees • specific AI systems • team members Instead, ISO certifications validate that the organization’s processes, governance, and development framework meet internationally recognized standards. For AI, this typically means: • The company follows responsible AI practices • It has risk management controls in place • It documents and monitors AI development properly • Its overall AI development lifecycle aligns with ISO standards (e.g., ISO/IEC 42001 for AI management systems) So the accreditation applies to the framework and processes, not people or specific ML models.
Option D explains that the company overall documents and monitors AI development appropriately, meaning all of the AI approved standards are followed responsibly.

question.en:
A company needs to apply numerical transformations to a set of images to transpose and rotate the images.

Which solution will meet these requirements in the MOST operationally efficient way?

text.en: Create a deep neural network by using the images as input.
Create an AWS Lambda function to perform the transformations.
Use an Amazon Bedrock large language model (LLM) with a high temperature.
Use AWS Glue Data Quality to make corrections to each image.

comment.en: Why Lambda is the MOST operationally efficient: • No servers to manage • Cheap and fast • Ideal for lightweight image manipulation • Can use Python libraries like Pillow or OpenCV • Automatically scales
The company only needs to apply simple numerical transformations — like transposing and rotating images — which are basic computational tasks, not machine learning or AI problems.
It requires simple numerical transformations/transposing tasks which can be achieved w/o using any AI/ML techniques here.

question.en:
A company is developing a generative AI application to automatically generate product descriptions for an ecommerce website. The product descriptions must consist of paragraphs of text that are consistent in style and tone. The application must generate thousands of unique descriptions each day.

Which type of generative model will meet these requirements?

comment.en: Diffusion model is used for image generation, not for text. Transformer-based models can maintain style and tone and scale to generate thousands of unique descriptions per day
This describes a system that needs to generate paragraphs of text that are consistent in style and tone — exactly what transformer-based models (like GPT, BERT, or T5) are designed for.

The task is to generate: • Paragraphs of text • With a consistent style and tone • At large scale (thousands per day) This is exactly what transformer-based models (like GPT, Llama, Claude, Titan, Nova Pro/Lite, etc.) are designed to do. Transformers excel at: • Natural language generation • Long-form content • Maintaining coherence, tone, and structure • High-throughput text generation They are the industry standard for generative text applications.

question.en:
A company is using a pre-trained large language model (LLM). The LLM must perform multiple tasks that require specific domain knowledge. The LLM does not have information about several technical topics in the domain. The company has unlabeled data that the company can use to fine-tune the model.

Which fine-tuning method will meet these requirements?

comment.en: Continued pre-training is used when: You want to expand the model’s knowledge base. You want the model to learn from unlabeled text. You need to adapt the LLM to a specific technical or industry domain.
Continued pre-training uses unlabeled domain-specific data to further train the model so that it can learn the terms, concepts, and knowledge of a specific domain.
C is correct

question.en:
A company is using a large language model (LLM) to create a generative AI assistant. The company must choose an AI technique to ensure that the AI assistant generates the most factually correct responses. The company selects the Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) technique.

Which limitation of LLMs is the company trying to reduce?

comment.en: Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) improves factual accuracy by retrieving relevant information from trusted external knowledge sources and supplying that information to the LLM before it generates a response. This method helps reduce the hallucinations issue to a great extent specially when the LLM model provides the confident response with inaccurate answers or generates incorrect information etc.

The correct answer is A. Hallucinations. In the context of generative AI, hallucinations occur when a large language model (LLM) generates responses that sound confident and fluent but are factually incorrect or completely fabricated. This usually happens because the model is predicting the next most likely word based on its training data rather than "looking up" real-time facts.

question.en: Which statement accurately describes Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG)?

text.en: A process that uses large amounts of new data to train large language models (LLMs) to improve LLM performance
A process by which large language models (LLMs) reference external authoritative knowledge bases to enhance the relevance and accuracy of LLM responses without re-training
A process that limits large language models (LLMs) exclusively to their original training data to improve response speed for business applications without re-training
A process that focuses on language translation tasks for businesses that operate in multiple countries

comment.en: Why B? Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) works by: - Retrieving relevant information from external data sources (documents, knowledge bases, vector databases, etc.). - Supplying that information as context to the LLM. - Generating a response grounded in the retrieved information.
B is the best option

The correct answer is B. A process by which large language models (LLMs) reference external authoritative knowledge bases to enhance the relevance and accuracy of LLM responses without re-training. Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) is a technique that bridges the gap between a model's general training and your specific, private, or real-time data.

question.en: Which task describes a use case for intelligent document processing (IDP)?

text.en: Analyze user feedback and perform sentiment analysis
Automatically extract and format data from scanned files

comment.en: Intelligent Document Processing (IDP) is used to: - Extract information from documents. - Process scanned forms, invoices, contracts, receipts, and PDFs. - Convert unstructured or semi-structured documents into structured data. - Automate document workflows. A common AWS service for IDP is Amazon Textract.

Intelligent Document Processing (IDP) is specifically designed to handle unstructured or semi-structured documents (like PDFs, scanned images, invoices, forms) and convert them into structured, usable data. It uses technologies like OCR, NLP, and machine learning to extract, classify, and process information.

question.en:

Which solution will meet these requirements?

comment.en: A. Amazon SageMaker Catalog

Amazon SageMaker Catalog helps organizations: - Discover and manage datasets. - Govern data assets. - Control access to approved data sources. - Ensure that training uses vetted and compliant datasets. This directly addresses the requirement to use only approved data. Tip: Govern and approve datasets -----> SageMaker Catalog

C. question.en:
A financial company stores patterns of fraudulent behavior in a database. The company uses this data to conduct investigations.

The company wants to use a graph-based ML solution to develop an AI tool that helps with these investigations.

Which AWS service will meet these requirements?

comment.en: Amazon Neptune is a graph database designed to: - Store and analyze relationships between entities. - Detect fraud rings and suspicious connections. - Perform graph analytics and graph machine learning. - Explore networks of accounts, transactions, devices, and users. Fraud investigations are a classic graph use case because relationships between entities are often more important than the entities themselves.

question.en:
A company runs an application on servers in an Amazon VPC. The company’s application uses Amazon Bedrock APIs for AI features. The company does not want API calls to travel across the public internet.

Which solution will meet this requirement?

text.en: Use AWS PrivateLink to establish a private connection between the Amazon VPC and Amazon Bedrock.
Sign API requests by using an access key ID and a secret access key that is associated with an IAM principal.
Move the application to an on-premises server. Make API calls to the public endpoint of Amazon Bedrock.
Encrypt the data in transit from clients to the APIs that have been implemented in the Amazon VPC. Encrypt the data in transit for API calls from the Amazon VPC to Amazon Bedrock.

comment.en: The requirement is: "The company does not want API calls to travel across the public internet." AWS PrivateLink provides private connectivity from a VPC to supported AWS services through VPC endpoints.
